analysis:
The only change in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift is at base line 795 / head lines 795-797. The text-path call to ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize now passes promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil. The commit comment says token reuse is partitioned exactly like the prefix KV cache. Relevant threat: T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle, SEC-035), which affects A-001.

Security reading: the change appears to add a tokenization-level reuse cache keyed by the coordinator-authored cache scope (the same value that feeds cacheSalt). When the cache is disabled, scope is nil, so tokenization should not reuse tokens. Using requestCacheScope, which is derived from the authenticated account, model build and prompt contract, matches the T-041 salt-scoping posture. I found no concrete regression in the supplied evidence.

Not visible in the supplied evidence: the implementation of ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize and its handling of promptCacheScope. Open questions for the next pass:
- Whether a nil scope truly disables any token-reuse cache, or falls into a shared global scope.
- Whether tokenization-cache keys are bounded and evicted, and whether they are retained in memory or on disk. If they were persisted, that would fall under T-041 detection_hint (no prompt-derived artifact beyond keyed tags).
- Whether scope isolation stops a same-account or cross-account timing oracle at the tokenization stage.
- Whether requestCacheScope is nil when it is not coordinator-authored, as in standalone mode.

The media path (lines 540-770) is unchanged. It does not pass promptCacheScope, and it uses separate prefix-identity logic. I flag no issue there. Further review of the tokenize implementation is recommended, since it is outside this batch.
